issues.headline: Work IQ agents get enterprise data and user memory

stories.label: WORK IQ FOR AGENTS
stories.text: Microsoft is bringing Copilot connectors to the Work IQ APIs and giving agents read access to a user’s Copilot memory.

image.alt: Microsoft's diagram of Work IQ: business data, context, memory and skills feeding Copilot and agents

stories.label: MIXED HARNESSES
stories.text: VS Code 1.145 lets one session mix agent harnesses: Claude can review a plan Copilot wrote, or Codex can run the same task alongside.

stories.label: CLAUDE ADMIN CONTROLS
stories.text: Claude Enterprise can now send every prompt and tool call through a company’s own security tools before it runs.

image.alt: Illustration of a hand holding a key, from Anthropic's announcement

stories.label: TEAMMATES IN SLACK
stories.text: Perplexity launched teammates: always-on agents you add to a Slack channel, where colleagues hand them work and ask for updates.

stories.label: NOTION AS CONTEXT
stories.text: Notion is repositioning as the shared context layer for every agent, including agents built by other companies.

image.alt: Chart from Notion's post: its MCP volume rising steeply through 2026

issues.deck: Also: VS Code mixes Copilot, Claude and Codex in one session, Claude gets security hooks before every tool call, Perplexity puts agents in Slack channels, and Notion wants to hold every agent’s context.

issues.headline: Salesforce brings Agentforce Coworker into Microsoft Teams

stories.label: COWORKER IN TEAMS
stories.text: Salesforce announced Agentforce Coworker for Microsoft Teams: an employee hands it a job in a Teams conversation and it coordinates Agentforce agents under the same Salesforce permissions and governance.

image.alt: Agentforce Coworker release art: a fuzzy blue bear-shaped character wearing sunglasses, with gold and teal sparkles on a blue background

stories.label: CLAUDE AS ISSUER
stories.text: Claude can now issue the signed identity assertions that MCP services use to recognize a company’s employees, so plugins connect with no per-user consent screen and no support needed from the company’s identity provider.

stories.label: KERNEL EXPLOIT PIPELINE
stories.text: OpenAI described an autonomous pipeline that found, validated and wrote patches for 948 local privilege-escalation vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel.

stories.label: CODING AGENT DEALS
stories.text: OpenAI will acquire Pierre Computer Company to expand the tools Codex has for building, understanding and reviewing code, on a day when two other coding-agent startups were also acquired.

stories.label: PERSONAL AGENT TRAFFIC
stories.text: Cloudflare launched analytics and per-agent access policies for personal agents, the assistants that browse, sign in and buy on a person’s behalf.

issues.deck: Elsewhere: Claude begins vouching for employees to MCP services, an OpenAI pipeline finds and patches Linux kernel flaws on its own, three coding-agent startups are acquired, and Cloudflare gives sites per-agent controls.

issues.headline: Half of Slack messages now come from apps and agents, Salesforce says

stories.label: SLACK BY THE NUMBERS
stories.text: Salesforce published Slack usage figures that show how much of the traffic is automated: 127 million MCP tool calls a week, doubling quarter over quarter.

image.alt: Slackbot and the Slack logo, with a human hand and a robot hand bumping fists

stories.label: AGENT KILL SWITCH
stories.text: CrowdStrike announced an AI Kill Switch in Falcon Guardian: an administrator can terminate a running agent, block it from relaunching and cut its network access.

stories.label: SIRI AI
stories.text: Apple opened Siri AI to all developers through a Developer Preview in the iOS, iPadOS, macOS and visionOS 27.3 betas.

image.alt: The Siri icon, a glowing glass orb on black

stories.label: PROVABLE INFERENCE
stories.text: Anthropic released FlashProve, an open-source prototype that lets a provider prove a response came from a specific model without revealing its weights. The post is dated November 2 and was announced on November 3.

image.alt: Illustration of steel chain links laid over paper textures

stories.label: AGENT CONFIG TRUST
stories.text: A developer’s bug report says Postman’s desktop app installed plugins into Claude Code and OpenAI Codex without asking. It was the most discussed developer story of the day.

issues.deck: The same day brought an agent kill switch from CrowdStrike, Siri AI for every developer, a way to prove which model produced an answer, and a coding-agent trust incident at Postman.

issues.headline: DeepSeek V4 ships 1M-token context as OpenAI releases GPT-5.5 and Codex goes autonomous

stories.label: DEEPSEEK V4
stories.text: DeepSeek V4 ships with native 1 million-token context support at no price premium, releasing two open-weight variants under MIT license on April 24.

stories.label: GPT-5.5
stories.text: OpenAI released GPT-5.5 on April 23 to Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise subscribers in ChatGPT and Codex, six weeks after GPT-5.4.

stories.label: ANTHROPIC POSTMORTEM
stories.text: Anthropic published a postmortem identifying three separate changes between March and April 2026 that degraded Claude Code quality, with all issues fixed in v2.1.116 on April 20.

stories.label: QWEN3.6-27B
stories.text: Alibaba released Qwen3.6-27B on April 22, an open-weight dense model that outperforms the larger Qwen3.6-397B MoE on agentic coding benchmarks.

stories.label: OPENAI CODEX
stories.text: GPT-5.3-Codex extends beyond code generation into debugging, deployment, testing, and monitoring, with full software lifecycle automation now available.

issues.deck: DeepSeek's V4 opens a million-token native context window at MIT-licensed open weights on the same day OpenAI ships GPT-5.5 to all paid subscribers and expands Codex into full software lifecycle automation. Alibaba's Qwen3.6-27B outperforms models 15x its size on coding benchmarks, and Anthropic publicly dissects three weeks of Claude Code quality degradation with specific dates, numbers, and a subscription reset for all affected users.

issues.headline: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and Canva all release agentic AI tools in a 24-hour window

stories.label: ANTHROPIC CLAUDE OPUS 4.7
stories.text: Anthropic released Claude Opus 4.7, scoring 64.3% on SWE-Bench Pro, nearly 10 points above Opus 4.6.

image.alt: Anthropic's illustration for Claude Opus 4.7: a node diagram beside a line drawing on a grid

stories.label: OPENAI CODEX DESKTOP AGENT
stories.text: OpenAI updated Codex on April 16, adding multi-agent workflows, desktop computer control, and 90+ plugin integrations.

stories.label: GOOGLE AI MODE IN CHROME
stories.text: Google shipped AI Mode directly into Chrome starting April 16 in the US, across desktop, Android, and iOS.

stories.label: CANVA AI 2.0 AGENTIC DESIGN
stories.text: Canva launched AI 2.0 on April 16 as a research preview for the first 1 million users, enabling text-to-design with persistent memory and workflow connectors.

stories.label: ALIBABA QWEN3 SPARSE MOE
stories.text: Alibaba released Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, a sparse MoE vision-language model with 35B total parameters but only 3B active at inference time.

issues.deck: Claude Opus 4.7 posts a 10-point SWE-Bench jump as OpenAI expands Codex into a desktop automation agent; Google embeds AI Mode directly into Chrome with side-by-side browsing; Canva launches a full agentic design platform with workflow connectors; Alibaba open-sources a sparse MoE model that activates just 3B of 35B parameters.

issues.headline: PrismML ships 1-bit LLMs that run in any browser

stories.label: PRISMML 1-BIT BROWSER LLMs
stories.text: PrismML released 1-bit Bonsai, a series of commercially licensed 1-bit quantized LLMs that run directly in WebGPU-enabled browsers with no Python, CUDA, or specialized hardware required.

stories.label: GOOGLE GEMINI 3.1 FLASH TTS
stories.text: Google launched Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS on April 15 with support for 70+ languages, 200+ audio control tags, and native multi-speaker dialogue generation.

stories.label: ANTHROPIC CLAUDE CODE DESKTOP
stories.text: Anthropic redesigned the Claude Code desktop app to support multiple concurrent agent sessions from a single window with persistent session management.

stories.label: CHINA HUMANOID FACTORY
stories.text: Leju Robotics and Dongfang Precision opened a factory in Foshan, Guangdong capable of producing 10,000 humanoid robots annually at one unit every 30 minutes.

issues.deck: PrismML's 1-bit Bonsai models bring sub-290MB inference to WebGPU browsers without Python or CUDA; Google launched Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS across 70 languages with 200+ audio control tags; Anthropic redesigned Claude Code desktop for parallel agent sessions; and Leju Robotics opened China's first automated humanoid factory at 10,000 units per year: while Hollywood's creative workforce reports a 50% income drop as studios accelerate AI adoption.

issues.headline: Anthropic buys Bun and Claude Code crosses $1B as Google ships Gemini Robotics-ER 1.6

stories.label: ANTHROPIC ACQUIRES BUN
stories.text: Anthropic acquired Bun, the all-in-one JavaScript runtime built by Jarred Sumner, to anchor the coding infrastructure behind Claude Code as the agent hit $1 billion in annualized revenue.

stories.label: GEMINI ROBOTICS-ER 1.6
stories.text: Google DeepMind released Gemini Robotics-ER 1.6, a robotics-focused embodied reasoning model with large gains in visual and spatial accuracy over ER 1.5, now available via Gemini API and Google AI Studio.

stories.label: OPENAI GPT-5.4-CYBER
stories.text: OpenAI announced Trusted Access for Cyber, an identity-verification program granting vetted cybersecurity professionals access to GPT-5.4-Cyber, a version of GPT-5.4 fine-tuned with lower refusal thresholds for defensive security work.

issues.deck: Anthropic acquired the Bun JavaScript runtime to power Claude Code as the coding agent crossed $1 billion in annualized revenue, while Google DeepMind released Gemini Robotics-ER 1.6 with a fourfold jump in instrument-reading accuracy, and OpenAI launched GPT-5.4-Cyber behind a tiered identity-verification program for security professionals.

issues.headline: Figma opens its canvas to agents as AWS ships AgentCore and LG releases a 33B open VLM

stories.label: FIGMA CANVAS AGENTS
stories.text: Figma released a native MCP server giving AI agents full write access to the Figma canvas, enabling creation and editing of components using a team's live design system.

image.alt: A terminal asking an agent to build a component set on the Figma canvas

stories.label: AWS AGENTCORE GA
stories.text: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore reached general availability alongside a Spring AI SDK, making production agent deployment native for Java/Spring developers.

stories.label: UK TRANSPORT GEMINI DEPLOYMENT
stories.text: The UK Department for Transport deployed a Consultation Analysis Tool built on Google Cloud Vertex AI with Gemini, cutting processing of 100,000+ public responses from months to hours.

stories.label: LG EXAONE 4.5 VLM
stories.text: LG AI Research released EXAONE 4.5, a 33-billion-parameter open-weight vision-language model targeting enterprise document understanding with a 262K token context window.

stories.label: SOFTR AI CO-BUILDER
stories.text: Softr launched an AI Co-Builder that generates fully functional business applications including database, UI, authentication, permissions, and third-party integrations from a single natural language prompt.

issues.deck: Figma gave AI agents write access to its live canvas via a native MCP server; AWS brought Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and a Spring AI SDK to general availability for Java developers; the UK Department for Transport published results showing Gemini cutting public consultation processing from months to hours; and LG AI Research released EXAONE 4.5, a 33-billion-parameter open-weight vision-language model that outscores GPT-5-mini and Claude 4.5 Sonnet on STEM benchmarks.

issues.headline: Lazarus Group compromised OpenAI's macOS signing pipeline via Axios npm attack

stories.label: OPENAI NPM SUPPLY CHAIN
stories.text: OpenAI confirmed that a malicious version of the Axios npm package (v1.14.1) executed inside its GitHub Actions workflow for macOS app-signing on March 31, 2026, exposing code-signing certificates for ChatGPT Desktop and Codex.

stories.label: ANDROID XR AUTO-SPATIALIZATION
stories.text: Google's April 2026 Android XR update for Samsung Galaxy XR headsets adds auto-spatialization, app pinning, session persistence, hand presence, and an expanded app ecosystem.

stories.label: VOXCPM2 OPEN-SOURCE TTS
stories.text: OpenBMB released VoxCPM2 on April 11, 2026, a 2-billion parameter tokenizer-free text-to-speech model under Apache-2.0 that runs on consumer hardware and supports 30 languages.

issues.deck: North Korea's Lazarus Group accessed OpenAI's code-signing certificates for ChatGPT Desktop and Codex through a poisoned Axios npm package, forcing a certificate revocation deadline of May 8; Google shipped auto-spatialization and persistent sessions to Android XR on Samsung Galaxy headsets; and OpenBMB released VoxCPM2, a 2B-parameter open-source TTS model covering 30 languages with voice cloning under Apache-2.0.

issues.headline: Amazon confirms $15B AWS AI revenue while agent platforms take shape

stories.label: Amazon AWS AI Revenue
stories.text: Andy Jassy's 2026 shareholder letter disclosed that AWS AI revenue crossed $15 billion annualized in Q1 2026, with Amazon's custom chip business generating over $20 billion annually.

stories.label: AWS Agent Registry
stories.text: AWS launched Agent Registry in preview as part of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, a centralized discovery and governance platform for AI agents, tools, and skills across enterprise environments.

stories.label: Anthropic Advisor Tool
stories.text: Anthropic released the advisor tool in beta, pairing Opus as an advisory model with Sonnet or Haiku executors in a single API call to improve benchmark performance while cutting costs.

stories.label: Perplexity Finance Hub
stories.text: Perplexity expanded its Plaid integration beyond investment accounts to checking, savings, credit cards, mortgages, auto loans, and student loans, enabling natural language queries over personal finances.

stories.label: France Exits Windows
stories.text: France's digital agency DINUM declared an official exit from Windows, requiring each ministry to formalize a Linux implementation plan by autumn 2026.

stories.label: Oxford Heart Failure AI
stories.text: Oxford researchers published an AI tool that predicts heart failure risk at least five years before onset using routine CT scans, detecting microscopic textural changes in cardiac fat tissue.

issues.deck: Andy Jassy put a $15B annualized number on AWS's AI business and defended $200B in capital expenditure, as AWS, Anthropic, and Perplexity each shipped new agent and finance infrastructure; France committed to a government-wide Linux exit by autumn 2026; and Oxford researchers published an AI tool that catches heart failure risk five years before onset.

issues.headline: Anthropic ships dual-model advisor API as Amazon discloses $15 billion AWS AI run rate

stories.label: ANTHROPIC OPUS ADVISOR API
stories.text: Anthropic shipped the advisor tool (beta header advisor-tool-2026-03-01) for the Claude API, enabling a dual-model architecture where Opus acts as an on-demand consultant to a Sonnet or Haiku executor.

image.alt: Anthropic's illustration for the advisor strategy: three linked nodes

stories.label: AMAZON AWS AI INFRASTRUCTURE
stories.text: Andy Jassy's 2026 shareholder letter disclosed that AWS AI has reached a $15 billion annual run rate, with Amazon's custom chip business generating over $20 billion annually.

stories.label: PERPLEXITY BANK INTEGRATION
stories.text: Perplexity expanded its Plaid integration beyond investment accounts to include checking, savings, credit cards, loans, and mortgages.

stories.label: AWS BEDROCK AGENT REGISTRY
stories.text: AWS Agent Registry, part of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, launched in preview on April 9 as a private, searchable catalog for agents, tools, skills, MCP servers, and custom enterprise resources.

stories.label: FRANCE LINUX TRANSITION
stories.text: France announced a government-wide transition from Windows to Linux, with every ministry required to submit implementation plans by autumn 2026, led by DINUM under a digital sovereignty mandate.

stories.label: OXFORD HEART FAILURE AI
stories.text: A team at the University of Oxford, led by Professor Charalambos Antoniades, published an AI tool that detects heart failure risk from routine CT scans by identifying microscopic textural changes in cardiac fat tissue.

issues.deck: Anthropic opened its Opus advisor API to developers, pairing high-capability reasoning with cheaper Sonnet or Haiku executors; Amazon's Andy Jassy put a $15B annual run rate on AWS AI and defended a $200B capex commitment; Perplexity hit $450M ARR with full bank account integration via Plaid; AWS launched a governed agent catalog inside Bedrock AgentCore; Oxford published an AI tool predicting heart failure five years early from CT scans; and France set a government-wide deadline to exit Windows for Linux.

issues.headline: Meta Superintelligence Labs ships Muse Spark, its first model, with a multi-agent deliberation mode built in

stories.label: META SUPERINTELLIGENCE LABS
stories.text: Meta Superintelligence Labs ships Muse Spark, a multimodal model (voice, text, image) with a "contemplating mode" that uses multi-agent deliberation to reason before responding.

stories.label: OPENAI: $100B ADS BY 2030
stories.text: OpenAI projects $100B in advertising revenue by 2030, with $2.5B targeted for 2026. An internal ad pilot already generated $100M in ARR in under two months.

stories.label: HEYGEN AVATAR V
stories.text: HeyGen launches Avatar V, addressing the identity-drift problem that caused AI video avatars to lose visual consistency over longer clips in earlier generations.

issues.deck: Meta's new Superintelligence Labs unit shipped its first model on Wednesday. Muse Spark handles voice, text, and image, and introduces a "contemplating mode" that routes queries through a multi-agent deliberation loop before responding. Meanwhile OpenAI mapped out a path to $100B in ad revenue by 2030, and HeyGen cracked the identity-drift problem that has plagued AI avatar video for years.

issues.headline: Anthropic's Mythos security model finds thousands of vulnerabilities but is restricted to 40 organizations due to its offensive capabilities

stories.label: ANTHROPIC MYTHOS: RESTRICTED RELEASE
stories.text: Anthropic withheld its Mythos security model from public release, granting access only to 40 organizations due to capabilities that far exceed any previous model in autonomous vulnerability discovery and exploitation.

stories.label: ANTHROPIC: 3.5GW COMPUTE
stories.text: Anthropic secured 3.5 gigawatts of compute capacity, a significant infrastructure commitment that signals confidence in sustained demand growth for its model portfolio.

stories.label: A16Z BACKS GITBUTLER
stories.text: a16z led GitButler's Series A, backing an AI-native Git client that rethinks version control workflows for the era of AI-assisted development.

issues.deck: Anthropic released Mythos Preview only to 40 handpicked organizations including AWS, Google, Microsoft, and Apple because the model's autonomous vulnerability discovery capabilities far exceed what can be safely deployed publicly. In testing, Mythos found a 27-year-old OpenBSD vulnerability, chained Linux kernel flaws for complete system takeover, and achieved an 83.1% first-attempt exploit success rate. Anthropic also locked in 3.5 gigawatts of compute capacity for scaling operations.

issues.headline: Sam Altman proposes a new social contract for ASI as Meta prepares to open-source its next model family

stories.label: ALTMAN'S ASI SOCIAL CONTRACT
stories.text: Sam Altman published a new framework for how OpenAI intends to approach artificial superintelligence, framing the company's obligations as a social contract with humanity rather than a set of technical safety constraints.

stories.label: META TO OPEN-SOURCE NEXT MODELS
stories.text: Meta is preparing open-source releases of versions of its next generation of AI models, extending its strategy of publicly releasing competitive weights while proprietary labs tighten access.

stories.label: ALTMAN FIRING MEMOS SURFACE
stories.text: The New Yorker published an investigative report surfacing internal documents and memos behind Sam Altman's November 2023 firing from OpenAI, adding new detail to the board's reasoning.

issues.deck: Sam Altman outlined a new framework for how OpenAI intends to govern the transition to superintelligence, framing it as a social contract rather than a technical milestone. Separately, Meta is preparing open-source releases of its next generation of models, continuing its strategy of matching proprietary labs on capability while keeping weights public. The New Yorker surfaced internal memos behind Sam Altman's 2023 firing, adding new detail to one of tech's most consequential governance crises.

issues.headline: Anthropic cuts off third-party agent platforms from Claude subscriptions, forcing migration to API pricing

stories.label: ANTHROPIC BLOCKS AGENT PLATFORMS
stories.text: Anthropic cut off agent platforms including OpenClaw from Claude subscriptions, citing capacity strain from agent workloads that run around the clock and consume far more tokens than chatbot use.

stories.label: NETFLIX VOID: PHYSICS VIDEO
stories.text: Netflix released VOID, an open-source framework that removes objects from video while rewriting the physics consequences across the scene, not just painting over the gap.

stories.label: GRANDCODE: 311 VOTES
stories.text: GrandCode is a multi-agent RL system using Agentic GRPO that took first place in three consecutive live Codeforces competitions, beating all human participants including legendary grandmasters.

issues.deck: Anthropic blocked platforms like OpenClaw from accessing Claude through flat-rate subscriptions, requiring them to pay via API or usage add-ons. Agent workloads consume far more tokens than typical chat use and were straining capacity. Netflix released VOID, open-source physics-aware video object removal that rewrites scene dynamics. On research: GrandCode beat all human participants including grandmasters in three consecutive live Codeforces competitions.

issues.headline: OpenAI makes its first media acquisition, buying live tech show TBPN, as a solo founder hits $1.8B in sales using only AI tools

stories.label: OPENAI ACQUIRES TBPN
stories.text: OpenAI acquired TBPN, a daily live tech talk show that pulls 70,000 viewers per episode and regularly hosts major tech CEOs, in its first media acquisition.

stories.label: $1.8B SOLO FOUNDER
stories.text: Matthew Gallagher launched Medvi, a telehealth startup, with $20K and AI tools including ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and Midjourney, reaching $1.8B in projected sales in 18 months.

stories.label: CALIFORNIA AI RULES
stories.text: Gov. Newsom signed an AI executive order and California legislators advanced multiple AI bills, making the state the de facto national standard-setter for AI regulation.

issues.deck: OpenAI acquires daily live tech talk show TBPN for a reported low hundreds of millions, its first media deal. Separately, Matthew Gallagher built Medvi telehealth to $1.8B projected sales with just $20K and AI tools, fulfilling Altman's 2024 solo-founder prediction. On the policy front, California becomes the de facto testing ground for AI regulation as Newsom signs an executive order and multiple bills advance in Sacramento.

issues.headline: Google releases Gemma 4 and ships free AI video in Google Vids with Lyria 3 and Veo 3.1

stories.label: GOOGLE GEMMA 4
stories.text: Google DeepMind released Gemma 4, its most capable open model family, built for advanced reasoning and agentic workflows with on-device deployment via HuggingFace Hub.

image.alt: Gemma 4 wordmark on a dark dotted pattern

stories.label: GOOGLE VIDS AI VIDEO
stories.text: Google Vids added free AI video generation powered by Lyria 3 for music and Veo 3.1 for footage, integrated directly into Google Workspace.

stories.label: HOLO3 COMPUTER USE
stories.text: H Company released Holo3, a model advancing autonomous GUI, browser, and desktop application operation by computer use agents.

stories.label: GEMINI API INFERENCE TIERS
stories.text: Google added Flex and Priority inference tiers to the Gemini API, letting developers trade response latency for lower cost.

issues.deck: Google DeepMind launched Gemma 4, its most capable open model family for agentic and multimodal tasks, while Google Workspace added free AI video generation via Lyria 3 and Veo 3.1. H Company pushed the computer use frontier with Holo3, and the Gemini API gained Flex and Priority inference tiers for cost and latency control. AWS published domain-restriction guidance for agent deployments, and HuggingFace papers showed strong community interest in simulation, RL credit assignment, and agent security.

issues.headline: FIPO tops HuggingFace with 330 votes as RL reasoning research dominates

stories.label: FIPO: RL REASONING
stories.text: FIPO reached 330 votes on HuggingFace, the day's top paper, proposing discounted future-KL divergence to improve credit assignment in RL training for language models.

stories.label: LONGCAT-NEXT: DISCRETE TOKENS
stories.text: LongCat-Next introduced a Discrete Native Autoregressive framework that represents text, image, and video in a shared discrete token space, enabling a single autoregressive model to handle all modalities.

stories.label: VLM REASONING DIVERSITY
stories.text: All Roads Lead to Rome identifies that RL-trained vision-language models collapse toward uniform reasoning patterns and proposes Multi-Group Policy Optimization to encourage diverse thinking strategies.

issues.deck: Reinforcement learning for deeper LLM reasoning led the research agenda on April 1, with FIPO, LongCat-Next, and three further papers covering multimodal reasoning, agent memory, and visual token efficiency all landing on HuggingFace. No major product announcements from the industry today.

issues.headline: Qatar's helium shortage puts AI chip fabs on a two-week clock

stories.label: Qatar Helium Crisis
stories.text: Missile strikes on Qatar's Ras Laffan facility shut down 30% of global helium supply, putting semiconductor fabs that produce Nvidia GPUs and HBM memory on a two-week countdown to shortages.

stories.label: Meta Hyperagents
stories.text: Meta released Hyperagents, implementing the Darwin-Godel Machine framework where a meta-agent rewrites the task agent's source code after failures, improving SWE-bench performance from 20% to 50% without parameter updates.

stories.label: Lilly x Insilico Deal
stories.text: Eli Lilly signed a $2.75B deal with Insilico Medicine to commercialize AI-discovered preclinical drug candidates, including a GLP-1 candidate.

stories.label: China Humanoid Robot Line
stories.text: UBTECH Robotics' Foshan facility went operational March 29, producing one humanoid robot every 30 minutes with capacity for 10,000 units annually.

issues.deck: Iranian missile strikes on Qatar's Ras Laffan facility cut 30% of global helium supply, threatening the Samsung and SK Hynix fabs that produce Nvidia GPUs and HBM memory; meanwhile Meta released Hyperagents for self-modifying AI agents, Eli Lilly committed $2.75B to commercialize Insilico Medicine's AI-discovered drugs, and China's first fully automated humanoid robot line went operational in Foshan.

issues.headline: Anthropic opens a research institute and signs a $200M deal with Snowflake

stories.label: Anthropic Institute
stories.text: Anthropic launched The Anthropic Institute, a dedicated policy and research body led by co-founder Jack Clark as Head of Public Benefit, consolidating three internal teams under a single structure.

stories.label: Snowflake Partnership
stories.text: Snowflake and Anthropic announced a multi-year, $200 million expanded partnership to power Claude-based agents inside Snowflake's enterprise data platform for over 12,600 global customers.

issues.deck: Anthropic launched The Anthropic Institute under co-founder Jack Clark to consolidate its policy and societal research, while a $200 million multi-year partnership with Snowflake embeds Claude Opus 4.5 and Sonnet 4.5 inside enterprise data workflows for 12,600+ global customers.

issues.headline: Sam Altman told OpenAI staff he tried to save Anthropic from Pentagon blacklist while his company took a competing defense contract

stories.label: OPENAI, ANTHROPIC, PENTAGON
stories.text: OpenAI announced a competing defense deal within hours of the Trump administration blacklisting Anthropic for refusing to sign a Pentagon contract without written prohibitions on mass surveillance and autonomous weapons.

stories.label: WHITE HOUSE AI FRAMEWORK
stories.text: The White House released a national AI legislative blueprint on March 21 calling for federal preemption of state AI laws, fracturing GOP consensus in Congress.

stories.label: GITHUB COPILOT TRAINING
stories.text: GitHub set an April 24 deadline for Copilot Free, Pro, and Pro+ users to opt out of interaction data being used to train AI models.

stories.label: GOOGLE STITCH
stories.text: Google shipped a major update to Stitch, its AI-native UI design tool, generating up to five interconnected screens from a text prompt and exporting working code to seven frameworks.

stories.label: COHERE TRANSCRIBE
stories.text: Cohere released cohere-transcribe-03-2026, a 2 billion parameter open-source speech recognition model under Apache 2.0 that tops the HuggingFace Open ASR Leaderboard.

issues.deck: A Pentagon blacklist of Anthropic and OpenAI's same-day competing defense deal set off internal backlash and a federal injunction, while the White House's new AI legislative blueprint fractured GOP unity in Congress. GitHub set an April 24 deadline for Copilot training opt-outs, Google shipped Stitch for free AI UI design, and Cohere released a 2B-parameter open-source transcription model that topped the HuggingFace ASR leaderboard.

issues.headline: CMS misconfiguration exposes Anthropic's unreleased Mythos, rated unprecedented cybersecurity risk

stories.label: ANTHROPIC MYTHOS LEAK
stories.text: Anthropic accidentally exposed a draft blog post about Claude Mythos through a misconfigured CMS, revealing its most capable model to date and confirming limited early-access testing is underway.

stories.label: MISTRAL VOXTRAL TTS
stories.text: Mistral Voxtral is a 4B-parameter open-weights TTS model, the first at production quality, available on Hugging Face under CC BY NC 4.0.

stories.label: GOOGLE GEMINI 3.1 FLASH LIVE
stories.text: Google Gemini 3.1 Flash Live is Google's highest-quality audio model, with lower latency than 2.5 Flash Native Audio, now rolling out to 200+ countries.

stories.label: AMAZON POLLY BIDIRECTIONAL STREAMING
stories.text: Amazon Polly adds bidirectional streaming, letting applications send text and receive audio simultaneously over a single connection without waiting for complete sentences.

stories.label: META TRIBE V2
stories.text: Meta TRIBE v2 is a foundation model trained on 500+ hours of fMRI recordings from 700+ people that predicts human brain responses to video, audio, and text.

issues.deck: A CMS misconfiguration exposed Anthropic's unreleased Claude Mythos, rated by the company as an unprecedented cybersecurity risk; on the same day, Mistral shipped the first open-weights TTS model at production quality, Google rolled out Gemini 3.1 Flash Live to 200 countries, and Amazon rewired Polly for token-streaming pipelines, while Meta published TRIBE v2, a brain-encoding model trained on 700 fMRI subjects.

issues.headline: ARC-AGI-3 exposes frontier AI adaptation gap as OpenAI rounds $120B and Google ships 6x memory compression

stories.label: ARC-AGI-3 BENCHMARK
stories.text: ARC-AGI-3 placed all frontier LLMs below 1% of human performance on interactive, goal-free reasoning environments, the benchmark's first major format change since 2019.

image.alt: ARC-AGI-3 title over a grid of puzzle game screens

stories.label: OPENAI FUNDING ROUND
stories.text: OpenAI's CFO confirmed an additional $10 billion close, pushing the total round past $120 billion at a $730 billion pre-money valuation.

stories.label: GOOGLE TURBOQUANT
stories.text: Google Research published TurboQuant, a two-stage algorithm delivering 6x KV-cache memory compression at 3-bit quantization with no measurable accuracy degradation and no retraining required.

stories.label: PENTAGON MAVEN AI
stories.text: The Pentagon designated Palantir's Maven Smart System as an official program of record, locking in multi-year funding with a $13.4 billion FY2026 AI budget line, up from $480 million in May 2024.

stories.label: OPENAI SAFETY BUG BOUNTY
stories.text: OpenAI launched a public Safety Bug Bounty targeting agentic product vulnerabilities including prompt injection, data exfiltration, and abuse patterns in Browser and ChatGPT Agent.

issues.deck: The ARC-AGI-3 benchmark placed every frontier model, from Google Gemini Pro to OpenAI GPT-5.4 High to Anthropic Claude Opus, below 1% of human performance on interactive reasoning, while OpenAI's funding round expanded to $120 billion at a $730 billion valuation, Google Research published TurboQuant delivering 6x KV-cache compression with zero accuracy loss, and the Pentagon formalized Palantir's Maven AI as a core military system with a $13.4 billion FY2026 budget.

issues.headline: OpenAI kills Sora and readies Spud as Anthropic, Mistral, and Apple expand their infrastructure positions

stories.label: OPENAI KILLS SORA, SPUD NEXT
stories.text: OpenAI is discontinuing Sora, the iOS app, API, and Sora.com, six months after launch, with freed compute redirected to Spud, its next major model family.

stories.label: ANTHROPIC $50B INFRASTRUCTURE
stories.text: Anthropic is committing $50B to U.S. AI infrastructure, building data centers in Texas and New York with Fluidstack throughout 2026.

stories.label: MISTRAL FORGE
stories.text: Mistral launched Forge at NVIDIA GTC, a platform that lets enterprises train fully custom AI models on proprietary data, training from scratch, not fine-tuning.

stories.label: APPLE BUSINESS APRIL 14
stories.text: Apple is merging Business Essentials, Business Manager, and Business Connect into a single unified platform launching April 14 in 200+ countries, with MDM now fully free.

stories.label: GOOGLE 2029 POST-QUANTUM DEADLINE
stories.text: Google published an accelerated timeline targeting full post-quantum cryptography migration across all systems by 2029, warning that "store now, decrypt later" attacks are already underway.

issues.deck: OpenAI is discontinuing Sora six months after launch and redirecting compute to its next model, Spud, while Anthropic commits $50B to U.S. data centers, Mistral launches Forge for training custom frontier models from scratch, Apple consolidates enterprise tools into a unified platform launching April 14, and Google sets a 2029 deadline for post-quantum cryptography migration across all systems.

issues.headline: Anthropic ships computer use, LiteLLM gets backdoored, and the enterprise agent land-grab accelerates

stories.label: ANTHROPIC COMPUTER USE
stories.text: Anthropic launched Computer Use in research preview for Claude Pro and Max subscribers, enabling Claude to click, type, open apps, and navigate browsers on macOS.

stories.label: LITELLM SUPPLY CHAIN ATTACK
stories.text: LiteLLM versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8, a library with 95M monthly PyPI downloads, contained a credential stealer embedded in a .pth file that executes on Python startup regardless of whether LiteLLM is imported.

stories.label: NVIDIA NEMOCLAW
stories.text: Nvidia announced NemoClaw at GTC, an open-source enterprise agent platform with sandboxed execution, least-privilege access controls, and infrastructure-layer policy enforcement.

stories.label: OPENAI FRONTIER ALLIANCES
stories.text: OpenAI formalized Frontier Alliances, multi-year partnerships with McKinsey, BCG, Accenture, and Capgemini to deploy its Frontier agent platform inside Fortune 500 companies.

stories.label: FIGURE 03 HUMANOID ROBOT
stories.text: Figure AI unveiled Figure 03, 9% lighter than its predecessor, with 2x faster actuators and tactile sensors detecting forces as small as 3 grams.

issues.deck: Anthropic turned its computer-use research into a shipping product for paying subscribers as LiteLLM's supply chain was compromised with a credential-stealing payload, while OpenAI, Nvidia, and Figure AI each pushed further into enterprise deployments, agent security infrastructure, and humanoid robotics production scale.

issues.headline: LiteLLM gets backdoored, Nvidia ships agent security infrastructure, and OpenAI winds down Sora

stories.label: LITELLM SUPPLY CHAIN ATTACK
stories.text: Threat actor group TeamPCP compromised LiteLLM's CI/CD pipeline and pushed credential-stealing malware to PyPI, exposing 97 million monthly downloads for 2–3 hours on March 23.

stories.label: NVIDIA NEMOCLAW
stories.text: Nvidia released NemoClaw at GTC 2026, a software stack adding enterprise security to OpenClaw agents with single-command installation.

stories.label: OPENAI SORA SHUTDOWN
stories.text: OpenAI announced the shutdown of the Sora app and API, citing compute costs and a strategic pivot toward robotics-focused world simulation research.

stories.label: FIGURE 03 HUMANOID ROBOT
stories.text: Figure 03 debuted in a live demo with reactive autonomy, performing autonomous package sorting with real-time disruption recovery using end-to-end neural networks.

stories.label: IPHONE 17 PRO, 400B MODEL ON-DEVICE
stories.text: A developer demonstrated Flash-MoE, a 400-billion parameter Mixture of Experts model, running entirely on-device on an iPhone 17 Pro with no internet connection.

issues.deck: TeamPCP's supply chain attack on LiteLLM exposed 97 million monthly PyPI downloads to credential theft; Nvidia countered the week's security narrative at GTC 2026 with NemoClaw, an open-source privacy and sandboxing layer for autonomous agents; while OpenAI shut down the Sora video app six months after launch to redirect compute toward robotics world simulation, Figure AI debuted Figure 03 with reactive autonomy at a $39B valuation, and a developer proved a 400B parameter model can run entirely on an iPhone 17 Pro.
